steps.title: Look at the four phrases again.
steps.sub: Keep going until you reach the crossroads. · Turn left. · Cross the road.
steps.prompt: What form does the person use to give a direction?
options: The imperative — the base verb, with no subject.
The Present Continuous — am, is or are with -ing.
A question with do — do you turn left here?
steps.answer: The imperative — the base verb, with no subject.
steps.why: Directions are given with the imperative: Turn left. Go past the bank. Cross the road. There is no you in it.

steps.title: Asking and giving directions
steps.html:
What you wantWhat you say
ask politelyCould you tell me the way to the station?
check a directionExcuse me, is this the right way to the library?
say “go forward”Go straight on. / Keep going until you reach…
say “change direction”Turn left. / Take the second turning on the right.
say “pass something”Go past the supermarket. / Cross the road.
say where it isIt’s on the corner, opposite the café.
reassure the personYou can’t miss it.

Ask with a polite question: Could you tell me…? / Excuse me, is this the right way to…? A bare Where is the station? sounds abrupt.

Give directions with the imperative: Turn left. Go past the bank.

Prepositions of movement carry the meaning: along, past, through, across, into, up to, until.

Finish with a landmark and a reassurance: It’s opposite the café. You can’t miss it.

You will meet the same polite question pattern again in Unit 7, Lesson 21, at a hotel reception.

steps.title: Text messages · model
steps.sub: The same directions, sent as text messages. You will write your own at the end.
steps.html:
Aida is coming to Timur’s flat

Aida · Hi — I’m at the bus station. Which way is it?

Timur · OK. Come out of the station and turn right. Then go straight on for about 200 metres.

Aida · Right at the exit?

Timur · Yes. Go past the big supermarket and cross the road at the traffic lights.

Aida · And then?

Timur · Take the second turning on the left, into Abay Street. My building is on the corner, opposite a small café. Green door, number 14.

Aida · How long does it take?

Timur · Ten minutes on foot. You can’t miss it.
